source.title: Noisy Weights: New Perspectives on Finding Noise-Robust Flat Minima
source.authors: P. Jacobson; B. Feinberg; T. Xiao; Christopher H. Bennett; S. Agarwal

record.file_problem: Text is a slide-deck transcription; some slide setup details and numerical results are absent, but the supplied text runs through the summary.
record.tranche_reason: Reports test accuracy, noise robustness, training dynamics, sharpness, and architecture comparisons under perturbative training. These results bear on the generalization-gap claim, though they focus on robustness to weight noise rather than the listed versions' core train/test error comparisons.
record.gate_note: The text does not report random-label fitting, natural-label train/test gaps, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected comparisons, optimizer held-out comparisons, batch size, dropout, or memorized-example removal. Training/test sharpness and noisy test accuracy are measurements relevant to the broad subject, but do not establish V7's specified magnitude-aware sharpness relation or any other listed version.
record.test_reason: The study measures robustness to weight noise, gradient behavior, and loss-landscape geometry. It does not test any listed version. In particular, it does not relate magnitude-scaled sharpness to ordinary train/test error gaps or compare generalization measures as V7 requires. The reference to SAM improving generalization is background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that SAM/RWP improve weight-noise robustness, large adversarial perturbations can disrupt learning through gradient attenuation, RWP is less affected, wider networks are more amenable to perturbative training, and ramping perturbations reduces this disruption and improves performance. They do not establish any listed generalization version.
record.recipe_differences: Studies robustness to weight/device noise using perturbative training methods (SAM/RWP), with training- and test-landscape measurements; it does not test the claim's specified natural-label generalization comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Training epoch; perturbation method and strength; gradient versus random direction; training versus test landscape; width versus depth; perturbation schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD and SAM peak in weight-noise robustness before convergence; RWP peaks at convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The timing of maximum weight-noise robustness depends on the training method.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM perturbed gradients have greater directional similarity to unperturbed gradients; large perturbations attenuate gradients, with a weaker effect for RWP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perturbation method and strength affect gradient direction and magnitude during training.

fits_no_version.finding: Sharpness depends on direction and evaluation data; SAM can have a sharp training trajectory and a flat test trajectory.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-landscape flatness alone does not characterize weight-noise robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: Wider ResNets have smoother landscapes and greater noise robustness under SAM/RWP than deeper ResNets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Network width versus depth affects robustness to weight noise under perturbative training.

fits_no_version.finding: Ramping perturbation strength reduces gradient attenuation and improves unspecified performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing perturbations gradually can mitigate training disruption from strong perturbations.

record.peer_reviewed: Sandia Machine Learning and Deep Learning Workshop (2025)
record.problems: The supplied slide text omits dataset/model setup details, quantitative values, error bars, and much of the plotted evidence. Several claims are qualitative; the architecture comparison does not map each listed model to its result.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Slide 9's result is retained only as figure-only because the supplied text gives no described outcome or numerical values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, strengths, and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking ordinary generalization gaps among comparably fitted networks, including comparison with norm and margin measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Assessment uses only the supplied slide transcription. Missing plots and setup prevent quantitative reconstruction. States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; several out-of-version qualitative findings are explicitly reported.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Whether widening past interpolation lowers test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance.
Large-batch training and its test-performance penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness predicting the train/test generalization gap.
Effect of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.
